text:
jordan: Posting a short thread — perf regression in KV cache observed on Qwen-medium across long contexts (~32k). Memory growth looks like repeated page allocations instead of reuse.

mike: Which run? can you paste perf profile and allocation traces?

jordan: Run id: run/2024-04-03-rt1. Quick snippet: shows `kv_alloc_pages++` spikes at token ~12k and ~20k. Paging counts increase even though same prefixes reused.

deepa: huh. Did kernel fallback or MQA path trigger? We had kernel selection change in last rollout.

jordan: Yes — kernel switch to `matmul_v3` for MQA paths at 03:15. Bisected to commit a1b2c3 -> kernel heuristics changed page rounding from 4k->8k which interacts w/ rope scaling.

lina: :thinking_face: Llama and Mistral don't show this, only Qwen variants and when GQA disabled. Might be a KV slot aliasing issue w/ MQA->GQA translation?

mike: Can you paste a mini repro? even a short command helps: `./run_infer --model qwen-7b --seq 32768 --profile=kvcache`

jordan: Repro steps: run above command w/ batch sizes 8/16/32, profile on. Grep outputs below:
```
# grep kvcache run.log
kvcache: page_alloc 132 -> 136 (+4)
kvcache: residency 0.72 -> 0.84
kvcache: reuse_hit 0.03
```

deepa: I think it's the batching heuristics: when batch sizes >16 we enable prefix folding which reorders page usage; combined with rope scale non-linear mapping causes fragmentation. Try disabling prefix folding.

lina: I'll run a quick experiment disabling the heuristic and toggling kernel. @mike can you check kernel-selection table for qwen model? maybe fallback metric is too sensitive.

mike: On it. quick note: kernel table has entry qwen-7b: prefer matmul_v3 for seq>8k. Fallback threshold uses `kv_page_density` which we recently adjusted. Rolling back that change removed similar regressions in Llama last month.

jordan: :thumbsup: Action items — (1) deepa run batch folding off reproducer, (2) lina run kernel toggle, (3) mike check telemetry and roll back kv_page_density tweak if confirmed. I'll create a small perf test to measure page churn and reuse ratio. tagging @perf-bot to schedule.

perf-bot: scheduled job perf/kv-churn-1741102233 for 2h starting in 30m

deepa: quick update — disabling folding reduced page_alloc spikes by ~60% on initial run. reuse_hit improved to 0.24. Still a small leak persists at tokens ~28k.

mike: Telemetry shows kernel_switch at 03:15 correlates with a second allocation wave. Might need to ensure KV pointer normalization across kernel variants (pointer tags + alignment).

jordan: Ok will instrument pointer tagging and report back. owner: jordan for the investigation.
